chapter: Early string bands and first jobs
title: Leonce's instruments and trombone playing; teachers
summary: Leonce moved from mandolin to guitar, string bass and trombone; Mello praises him and names other trombonists he played with, then mentions Father Reuther at Holy Cross as a teacher.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers

And, uh, he was good. I'm going to tell you what I know. Not that he's my brother, was my brother, but I'll hold his end up any time, because you can take a few fellas that knew Lawrence, and they'll tell you what kind of trombone player he was. He was a trombone player. I played with some good trombone players. I played with Eddie Benton, I played with Eddie Riley. I played with, uh, Humpback Gallaty. Now, Bill Gallaty wasn't much of a slide man, but he was a pretty good tenor trombone player. That's Val? Val. Tenor. Val. He's the first one, Leonce is the first one that I can remember of. He played bass one night and he filled in on for a fella, I don't know who got sick. He filled in for a fella and I see him with a drumstick in his pocket. He said, what did he play drums too? He said, no, I'm going to pick a bass. I'm going to pick a bass with a drumstick. He said, you don't think that I'm going to bust up all my fingers, he says, picking on strings. And we used to tune up B-Natural. We used to tune up on high pitch, not no low pitch, high pitch. When you start picking on a string bass, I mean make it slap. I don't mean boom, boom, boom like they're picking out and just pick on the strings like that. I mean make it slap and you got some way. No, it's just a bit of a picnic sometimes. Got it all there.
